verifiedStaticFacts.fact: Spacing sorts living bodies by ID, uses antisymmetric ID-hashed directions for coincident centers and does not consume gameplay RNG. Planning returns a map before host application.

Source/core bodies, any body with committed attackAt and current pursuing migration carriers are excluded from spacing movement. Dead bodies are ignored as spacing neighbors. Other bodies yield to fixed bodies.

The relaxation budget incorporates trait speed, slow factor, fixed step and explicit1.25 separation factor. Candidate relaxation moves are checked against static footprint/bounds and displacement budget. A successful spacing move skips the subsequent pursuit step. Pursuit still uses the shared static collision projector, with legal/budget checks for alternate tangents.

Host applies planned positions before the enemy phase. Committed attacks are not moved by spacing on their resolve tick; the existing impact path reads attackAim/attackTarget before clearing them. The new spacing module does not write HP, attack timing, aim, trait or actor role. MIMIC keeps its tissue goal and trait slowdown; elites remain eligible for spacing when not committed.
Living actor insertion paths retain the24-actor cap. Crowd helpers neither spawn nor delete actors; their neighbor arrays filter current living bodies.

complexity.spacing: For L living bodies and M static obstacles, bounded candidate count gives O(L² + L·M + L log L), plus filtering the stored target array. Each movable body can score up to5 collision-projected candidates against living neighbors.
complexity.pursuit: Each pursuit call filters/sorts neighbors and may check forward plus6 tangent candidates. Across the enemy tick, repeated per-body sorting/checking is above O(L), at most O(L² log L + L·M) for fixed candidate counts, plus target-array filtering.
complexity.bounds: L is bounded by24 in actual insertion paths. This bounds work; it does not itself prove a real-browser frame budget.
complexity.finding: Concrete static cost description only. No measured FPS regression or mandatory optimization is asserted without current real-browser evidence.
